subject: Intermittent 503s + p95 latency spike (us-west) — routing mitigation in progress
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@stratus.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <ops@stratus.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Stratus AI - intermittent 503s & p95 spike (us-west)

Hi Sean / Marissa,

We're seeing repeated 503s and a sustained p95 jump (~1.1s -> 2.9s) originating from us-west over the last ~45 minutes. Scope: our inference calls to /v1/generate (model: gptx-14k) are affected; sample request IDs attached (request-samples.txt). Impacting production traffic for a subset of customers — visible errors in our service graph and retries piling up.

Can you confirm whether there's a known degradation in us-west and whether you can route our traffic to another region while you investigate? We're sensitive to session affinity but can tolerate short-lived redirect for the next 2 hours if it helps reduce error rates.

Thanks —
Alex
Principal SRE, Stratus AI
attachments: request-samples.txt
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@stratus.ai>, SRE Team <ops@stratus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:11:30 +0000
Subject: Re: Stratus AI - intermittent 503s & p95 spike (us-west)

Hi Alex — thanks for the report and the sample IDs. We’re seeing elevated error rates and queue growth in the us-west inference pool and have opened INC-20270920-usw1 on our status page (https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20270920-usw1).

Immediate plan: with your approval we can shift ~95% of your production traffic to our us-east pool using a routing override for the next 1-2 hours while we triage. This will minimize request retries and stabilize p95 while preserving a small fraction of traffic to monitor any session-affinity regressions. Attached is the short traffic-shift-plan.pdf documenting the change and rollback steps.

If you’re OK with that, I’ll execute the override now and keep you updated every 15 minutes. We’ve looped in Marissa (Customer Ops) and Ben (Escalations) for coordination and postmortem follow-up.

—Sean
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
attachments: traffic-shift-plan.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:22:45 +0000
Subject: Re: Stratus AI - intermittent 503s & p95 spike (us-west)

Alex — thanks, we’ll proceed with the routing override now and will monitor.

What we’ve done (09:22 UTC):
- Shifted ~95% of Stratus AI production traffic to us-east using a customer routing override.
- Enabled elevated logging and request-id tracing for your account.
- Opened a dedicated investigation runbook and captured the sample request IDs you provided.

Preliminary customer-visible impact: error rate dropped to near-baseline within ~6 minutes of the shift; p95 returned to ~1.15s. We will continue to monitor for session-affinity issues and will keep the override in place until we complete the RCA and confirm stability.

We attached the diagnostic bundle (diag-logs.zip) and are preparing an initial incident timeline for you. Expect a full postmortem within 48 hours.

Regards,
Marissa
Sr. Customer Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: diag-logs.zip
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@stratus.ai>, SRE Team <ops@stratus.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 18:15:00 +0000
Subject: Postmortem: INC-20270920-usw1 — routing mitigation & RCA

Alex / Stratus team — apologies again for the disruption. Below is the final postmortem and the steps we’ve taken to prevent recurrence.

Summary
- Impact: intermittent 503s and elevated p95 for inference requests served by our us-west pool between 2027-09-20T08:35Z and 2027-09-20T09:22Z. Affected endpoint: /v1/generate for model gptx-14k.
- Mitigation: we executed a routing override at 2027-09-20T09:22Z that shifted ~95% of Stratus AI traffic to us-east; error rates returned to baseline within 6 minutes.

Root cause
- A scheduling regression in our control plane release (rev 4.7.2) caused inefficient placement decisions for long-lived KV caches under certain memory pressure patterns. That led to elevated cache evictions and queue growth in the us-west inference pool, which in turn caused timeouts and 503 responses when workers fell behind re-populating KV caches.

Actions taken
- Deploy hotfix to scheduling logic (rolled 2027-09-21T03:40Z) — fix validated in canary and promoted to production.
- Expanded us-west inference pool capacity by 12% during the outage window to reduce immediate queuing pressure.
- Added a control-plane healthgate that prevents scheduling changes from applying to pools with >20% active KV eviction rates.
- Improved alerting: new metric alerts for KV eviction rate and queue length anomalies with 60s burn-in.
- Customer-facing: we kept the routing override in place for Stratus AI until 2027-09-20T12:05Z to validate stability; no session-affinity regressions reported.

Compensation
- We’re offering a one-time service credit equivalent to 5% of September usage charges for the impacted account; Marissa will coordinate the credit.

Attachments and links
- postmortem-summary.pdf (attached)
- Incident timeline and raw diagnostic bundle: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20270920-usw1
- HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/record/HS-987654321

Next steps
- Weekly follow-up: Kim will run an on-call review with the infra releases team to ensure the new gate remains effective for the next 4 releases.
- We’ll share a short engineering note on the scheduling change and monitoring dashboards.

If you prefer a quick call to walk through the timeline and technical details, we’re available and happy to schedule.

Sincerely,
Ben Carter
Head of Escalations, Redwood Inference
attachments: postmortem-summary.pdf
